items.title: Emergence of the FLAIR Ivy Sign During Progressive Posterior Cerebral Artery Occlusion and Postoperative Disappearance After Revascularization Surgery in Adult Moyamoya Disease: A Case Report
items.authors: Mugikura S, Mori N.
items.label: Figure 2
items.caption: Imaging findings during the compensated collateral phase. A woman in her 40s with moyamoya disease had previously undergone left superficial temporal artery–middle cerebral artery (STA–MCA) bypass surgery with additional indirect revascularization for ischemic symptoms involving the left cerebral hemisphere and remained neurologically stable during long‐term follow‐up. (A) Axial magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) obtained 9 years after left‐sided bypass surgery demonstrates bilateral steno‐occlusive changes of the internal carotid arteries (ICAs), consistent with moyamoya disease. The left STA–MCA bypass graft is patent, and extracranial‐to‐intracranial collateral flow supplying the left cerebral hemisphere is well preserved (blue arrows). Mild narrowing is observed in the proximal portion of the right posterior cerebral artery (PCA) (red arrow), while distal PCA branches remain well visualized, suggesting preserved PCA–derived leptomeningeal collateral supply to the anterior circulation. No significant steno‐occlusive changes are observed in the left PCA. (B) Axial fluid‐attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) imaging obtained at the same examination demonstrates no FLAIR ivy sign in either cerebral hemisphere. Old ischemic lesions are observed predominantly in the bilateral periventricular deep white matter, consistent with previous ischemic injury. Diffusion‐weighted imaging showed no acute ischemic lesions (not shown).

items.title: Florid Cemento-Osseous Dysplasia Associated With Simple Bone Cysts: Radiographic Evolution Over 13 Years-A Case Report
items.authors: da Silva de Oliveira F, Silva VT, Santos LR, de Lima ABR, Sugaya NN, Júnior CAL.
items.label: Figure 2
items.caption: Cone‐beam computed tomography (CBCT) demonstrating multiple bilateral radiolucent intraosseous cavities in the mandible. (A) Panoramic reconstruction showing the bilateral posterior cavities. (B–G) Selected representative cross‐sectional images of the right posterior cavity, corresponding to the edentulous region of Tooth 46, demonstrating its buccolingual extent and thinning of the buccal and lingual cortical plates. The right posterior cavity measures approximately 19 × 10 × 14 mm in the anteroposterior, buccolingual, and superoinferior axes, respectively.
